title: 🎖️ Poland Signs a $300 Million Deal with Palantir — AI to Guide Army Decisions!
body: 🎖️ Poland Signs a $300 Million Deal with Palantir — AI to Guide Army Decisions!
Poland has signed an agreement with Palantir worth about $300 million over five years, to buy AI software that helps army leaders make decisions.
The system is called Maven Smart System, and it will operate in Poland under the name Saturn, merging data from drones, satellites, and radars into a single operational picture.
The system analyzes this data to identify targets, manage battlefield information, and suggest response options, while the final decision remains in the hands of human commanders.

Poland's defense minister confirmed that all keys, servers, and information will remain the exclusive property of the Polish Armed Forces, and that the company will have no remote access to military data.
The deal follows cooperation that began in 2025, at a time when European countries are racing to bring AI into their armies, amid concern about overreliance on American technology.
Simply put: AI is entering the army's command rooms — should the final military decision always stay in human hands?
Would you trust AI systems that make decisions on the battlefield?
